finding.claim: The DELETE /reports/:id handler calls the async authorize() without await, so the permission check never blocks the deletion. A user without the delete grant can delete any report. If authorize() rejects, the rejection is unhandled and the delete still runs.
finding.source: Any request to DELETE /reports/:id with any report id. This includes users who have no 'delete' grant on that report. Even an unauthenticated request works if req.session exists, because the failed check is not awaited.
finding.sink: db.reports.remove(report.id) at server.js:21, the destructive operation that deletes the report.

trace.note: DELETE /reports/:id route handler, reachable by any HTTP client on port 3003
The report is loaded by the attacker-supplied req.params.id
authorize(req.user, 'delete', report) returns a Promise that is neither awaited nor returned. Execution continues immediately.
Inside authorize, the grants lookup is async and the 403 Error is only thrown after it resolves. By then the handler has moved on.
await db.reports.remove(report.id) runs without waiting for the authorization result
Responds 204 even when authorization would have failed

finding.guards_checked: The authorize() implementation is correct, since it throws 403 when the grant is missing. The sibling PUT handler awaits it at server.js:27, so the intended control exists but is not enforced on DELETE. No other middleware does authorization. The global middleware at lines 4-7 only copies req.session.user and checks nothing. There is no try/catch or error handler that would stop the remove call. Because the rejection from the un-awaited promise is unhandled, it can also crash the process on Node 15+ (unhandled rejection), a secondary DoS. Reproduction: curl -X DELETE http://host:3003/reports/<id> as a user with no delete grant, which returns 204 and the report is gone. The same request to PUT returns 403.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 throws 403 correctly, but its Promise is discarded at server.js:20. There is no other middleware, try/catch or error handler. The middleware at lines 4-7 only copies the session user.
verdict.reason: server.js:20 calls async authorize() without await, so the rejection from lines 11-14 never stops db.reports.remove at server.js:21, while the PUT handler awaits it at server.js:27. Any authenticated low-privilege user can therefore delete any report. The "unauthenticated" claim is slightly overstated, since it needs req.session to exist (server.js:5).
